newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent crude ends weaker but suppported.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent crude ends weaker but suppported.

text.p: IPE Brent futures ended weaker forging fresh lows on late selling pressure but support around $22.60 a barrel managed to hold.
Cold weather, expectations that OPEC will freeze its current ceiling and the unlikelyhood of any "quick fix" Iraqi oil sale prevented a massive selloff, traders said.
"We are not going to see the (Iraqi) oil on the market for at least three months whatever happens," a broker said.
The Jan Brent contract last traded 42 cents a barrel lower at $22.61.
Traders said the market was well supported fundamentally by tight prompt crude supply and good refining margins, with winter demand for gas oil expected to remain firm.

Earlier though it tumbled around 35 cents a barrel when Iraqi U.N. ambassador Nizar Hamdoon said Baghdad had agreed to all U.N. conditions that had held up the implementation of the oil for food sales deal.

This statement was followed up by a senior U.S. official, Edward Gnehm, saying he saw no problem with the pricing formula for the Iraqi oil sales and a U.N. statment later said Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali expected some movement in the next few weeks, although there was still some work to be done.
Both later statements were met with limited interest and neither pushed the market down further.
"People traded off the Iraq agreement to terms but most players are still sceptical the sale will go ahead quickly," a broker said.
The December gas oil contract last traded $3.75 a tonne down at $219.00.
